lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Check that the LinkedIn URL works and points to your profile.
Remove the date of birth and nationality unless an application requires them.
items.because: They generally do not help a U.S. resume.

items.says: Replace “Metro City” if it is a placeholder.
items.because: The education entry should give the actual location.

items.says: Put Brightcart before Pinecrest.
items.because: The most recent job should appear first.

items.says: Account for the period since Brightcart ended in June 2025 if there is relevant activity to show.
Do not present stopping at the first daily p-value below 0.05 as a sound A/B testing method.
items.because: Repeated peeking can inflate false positives.

items.says: Explain the decision the A/B test informed.
Clarify what “checkout” means in an insurance context.
Clarify how you established that the shift change caused the hold-time reduction.
items.because: Another factor may have caused the reduction.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
Specify the period or basis for the “by half” reduction.
Separate the automation achievement from the unrelated duties.
items.because: The combined bullet makes it hard to tell which work saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.

items.says: Clarify whether the dashboard or a campaign using it drove the increase.
items.because: The full change should not be assigned to the dashboard without supporting evidence.

items.says: Express the rise from 22% to 27% as 5 percentage points.
Specify whether the two hours include review and validation, if relevant.
items.because: The before-and-after comparison should be like-for-like.

items.says: Correct the query logic for identifying customers with no orders.
items.because: A null customer name does not reliably identify them; the test must use a field from the unmatched orders side.

items.says: Add the business use or result.
items.because: The bullet currently describes a basic query without an outcome.

items.says: Make the action grammatically consistent with the other bullets.
Clarify what “tied to a campaign” measures.
items.because: A higher match rate does not, by itself, mean attribution became more accurate.

items.says: Identify the type of recommendations funded or their subsequent effect, if possible.
Specify the timeframe or source for the halving of requests, if available.
Define the forecast-error metric and how it was calculated.
items.because: “12% mean absolute error” mixes a percentage with a metric usually expressed in demand units.

items.says: Label the empty-station result clearly as a replay or simulation.
items.because: It should not read as an observed operational reduction.

items.says: Correct the reduction from 300 to 200 to 33%, not 50%.
Define a forecast “hit” and distinguish hit rate from the error metric above.
Express the rise from 60% to 75% as 15 percentage points or 25% relative, not simply 15%.
Clarify whether the line figures are measured averages.
Clarify whether other changes occurred at the same time.
items.because: Those changes could have affected the shorter line.

items.says: Make sure “9,000” refers to logs or records rather than visits, if those differ.
Consider cutting the update-guide bullet if ongoing handoff does not matter to the target roles.
items.because: It is the first project bullet the review would cut for space.

items.says: Match the listed tools to the jobs you want and name dbt if you used it.
items.because: Do not imply tool experience you lack.

items.says: Match the listed methods to the jobs you want.
